The Turán graph T(14,2) = K(7,7) is the densest triangle-free graph on 14 vertices, and it's also maximal (it's a complete bipartite graph, so adding any edge within a partition creates a triangle).

K(7,7) is a complete bipartite graph with parts {0,1,2,3,4,5,6} and {7,8,9,10,11,12,13}.

Every vertex in {0,...,6} connects to every vertex in {7,...,13}, giving 7×7 = 49 edges.

This is triangle-free because all edges go between the two parts, and any triangle would need two edges within a part.

It's maximal because adding any edge within {0,...,6} or within {7,...,13} would create a triangle (the two endpoints both connect to all vertices in the other part).
